Theme

Body, health & movement

high adjective

on drugs

also get high, be high, stoned (on drugs), high on drugs, trip (drug-induced)

classical

Traupman 328: on alcohol or drugs
M-O s.v. intoxicated, high

ēbrius, ēbria, ēbrium

drunk; high (on drugs)

The classical word for drunk, stretched to drugs, as Traupman and Morgan–Owens do; English “intoxicated” covers both in the same way.

Other words

  • medicāmentīs psychotropicīs inēbriārī — get high on drugs

    modern · Plin. NH 12.103: palma vescentēs inēbriat (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. intoxicate: inēbriārī, get high

    inēbriō is to make drunk (Pliny, Seneca), so getting high is the passive, with the drug in the ablative of means.

  • ā medicāmentīs psychotropicīs inēbriāre — Traupman: be high on drugs

    avoid · modern · Traupman 328

    The active inēbriāre means to make someone drunk, not to be drunk, and ā marks a person as agent, not a thing; say medicāmentīs psychotropicīs inēbriārī.

See also drunk, drug, drug addict.

SourcesLewis & Short: ebrius · Lewis & Short: inebrio
